chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Qur’an is the covenant of Allah to His creatures, it is incumbent therefore on a Muslim man to look into his covenant and that he recite fifty verses from it every day
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended daily amount of Qur'an recitation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the Qur’an is elevated as the divine covenant ('ahd) entrusted to humanity, emphasizing the believer's duty to actively engage with this testament through reflection and consistent recitation. The specific prescription of fifty verses daily underscores the importance of regular, manageable engagement with the text to maintain spiritual connection, a practice rooted in the Imami tradition of daily dhikr and tafsir. This guidance highlights the Qur’an not merely as a book to be read, but as a living agreement requiring ongoing personal review.

en.ammaar-muslim: [1/1551] al-Kafi: Ali from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:
The Qur’an is the covenant of Allah to His creatures, it is incumbent therefore on a Muslim man to look into his covenant and that he recite fifty verses from it every day
